---
title: "Deployment"
description: "How Polydelve ships: rolling deploys, AWS topology, and ETL scheduling."
---

## Deploy strategy

Polydelve uses a **rolling deploy**. There are no active users, so zero-downtime guarantees (canary, blue-green) add complexity with no benefit. The backend runs as an `aws_ecs_express_gateway_service`, which manages rollout behavior internally (no `min_healthy_percent` is set in Terraform).

Canary and blue-green deploys are explicitly out of scope for this project.

## AWS topology

```
Internet
  └── CloudFront (CDN / TLS termination)
        └── Backend API (ECS Fargate — Dockerized)
              └── RDS Postgres
```

- **CloudFront** — serves the frontend (S3 origin) and proxies `/api/*` to the backend.
- **Backend API** — runs the FastAPI app inside a Docker container on ECS Fargate.
- **RDS Postgres** — primary datastore; Alembic manages schema migrations.

Terraform manages provisioning. Full reference: [Infrastructure](/docs/build/infrastructure).

## Shipping a backend release

<Steps>

<Step>
**Build image** from `backend/Dockerfile`:

```bash
docker build -t polydelve-backend:$TAG ./backend
```
</Step>

<Step>
**Push** to ECR (or your configured registry):

```bash
docker push $ECR_REPO/polydelve-backend:$TAG
```
</Step>

<Step>
**Update ECS service** — force a new deployment so ECS pulls the new image:

```bash
aws ecs update-service \
  --cluster polydelve \
  --service polydelve-backend-v3 \
  --force-new-deployment
```

In practice, use `scripts/deploy-backend.sh` (`make deploy-be`) — it builds, tags, pushes to ECR, and forces the deployment in one step.
</Step>

<Step>
**Run migrations** if the release includes schema changes:

```bash
cd backend && DATABASE_URL=<rds-url> uv run alembic upgrade head
```

The deploy script does not run migrations. RDS only accepts connections from inside the VPC, so temporarily allowlist your IP (see [Infrastructure](/docs/build/infrastructure#rds-access)) or run the command as an ECS task override. Run it before or right after the new task starts, depending on whether the change is backward-compatible.
</Step>

</Steps>

The backend image is tagged `latest` (or `$IMAGE_TAG`) and rolled out by `--force-new-deployment`. Env vars, secrets and resource limits are managed via Terraform. See [Infrastructure](/docs/build/infrastructure) for the full resource reference.

## ETL job scheduling

ETL jobs run via `python -m etl.run <job>` (see `backend/etl/run.py`). The primary scheduler is **EventBridge Scheduler** — a Fargate task runs at 9am, 12pm, and 5pm ET executing the `refresh` composite job. Individual jobs can also be triggered manually or via CI.

| Cadence | Command | What it does |
|---------|---------|--------------|
| 9am, 12pm, 5pm ET (EventBridge) | `refresh` composite | EPSS refresh + news + MAL advisories + CVE history, then resolves contracts |
| On-demand | `make etl-epss` | Refresh EPSS scores from the daily bulk file |
| On-demand | `make etl-news` | Fetch security news, generate + rerank featured contracts |
| On-demand | `make build-cve-history` | Backfill CVE history for all tracked packages (`etl.run cve`) |
| On-demand | `make etl-packages` | Refresh package metadata (downloads, risk score) |
| On-demand | `make resolve-contracts` | Resolve open contracts (wins + expiries), credit bits |

See [Data Pipeline](/docs/build/data-pipeline) for the full ETL architecture and bootstrap order.

## Infrastructure

Terraform provisions and manages all AWS resources (CloudFront, ECS, RDS, ECR, IAM, DNS, ACM). Full reference: [Infrastructure](/docs/build/infrastructure).
